description: Indulge in the ultimate American breakfast experience with these unbelievably fluffy buttermilk pancakes. Each bite offers a light, airy texture with a subtle tang, making them the perfect canvas for your favorite toppings. This recipe ensures a golden-brown stack that will bring joy to any morning.

instructions.title: Prepare Dry Ingredients
instructions.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the sifted all-purpose flour, granulated sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. Ensure all dry ingredients are well combined to prevent lumps later.

instructions.title: Combine Wet Ingredients
instructions.text: In a separate medium bowl, whisk together the buttermilk, large eggs, melted unsalted butter, and vanilla extract until smooth. Make sure the butter is not too hot, or it might cook the eggs.

instructions.title: Mix Batter Gently
instructions.text: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients. Stir gently with a whisk or spatula until just combined. It is crucial not to overmix; a few lumps are perfectly fine and will contribute to the pancakes fluffiness.

instructions.title: Rest the Batter
instructions.text: Let the pancake batter rest for 5-10 minutes at room temperature. This allows the gluten to relax and the baking powder and soda to activate, leading to a lighter, fluffier pancake.

instructions.title: Cook the Pancakes
instructions.text: Heat a lightly oiled or buttered griddle or large non-stick skillet over medium-low heat. Pour about 1/4 cup of batter per pancake onto the hot griddle. Cook for 2-3 minutes per side, or until golden brown and bubbles form on the surface before flipping. Adjust heat as needed to prevent burning.

instructions.title: Serve Your Stack
instructions.text: Transfer cooked pancakes to a plate and serve immediately. For a warm stack, you can keep finished pancakes warm in a low oven (around 200F / 95C) while you finish cooking the rest. Serve with your favorite toppings like maple syrup, fresh berries, or whipped cream.

tips: Do not overmix the batter; lumps are your friend for fluffy pancakes. Overmixing develops gluten, leading to tough pancakes.

For extra richness, brown your butter before adding it to the wet ingredients. If you dont have buttermilk, you can make a quick substitute by adding 1 tablespoon of white vinegar or lemon juice to regular milk and letting it sit for 5 minutes.
Serve pancakes immediately for best texture. Leftover pancakes can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days and reheated in a toaster or microwave.
